question: Does a first-party primary-paper table provide a reproducible historical TRI-X density-dependent Wiener-granularity amplitude observation that can constrain future generic B&W structure research without being relabeled as current 400TX?

source.title: Information Capacity of Photographic Films
source.author: R. Clark Jones
source.journal: Journal of the Optical Society of America 51(11), 1159-1171

branch_rule.pass: retain a historical density-dependent Wiener-amplitude source prior and open only a separately frozen generic amplitude-shape compatibility test
branch_rule.fail: close this source route without substituting secondary tables or current-stock labels

claim_ceiling: Historical primary-paper density/Wiener-amplitude observations for Eastman TRI-X type 5233 developed 6.5 minutes in SD-28; not current Kodak 400TX, D-76, modern coating, NPS shape, scanner response, roll calibration, photographic appearance or product evidence.
